flagship_directive: Push the affine-hull plus Gram-diagonal reduction past the threshold slope: prove a leverage-only closed form for the full curve \(v^*(\rho;S)\) (hence \(\kappa(S)\)) for arbitrary \(S\), or at minimum close the \(p/(n-1)\) gap in the regret bracket to an exact \(R^*(n,S)\) for rank-one score spaces, eliminating the exponential sign-pair program where it currently carries the general case.
critique: The one genuinely new kernel is \ref{thm:admissibility-frontier}: the affine-hull identification of \(\gamma(S)\) with \(\min\{\lambda_{\max}(K|H_n):K\mathbf1=0,\operatorname{diag}K=\operatorname{diag}P_S\}\) plus the zero-sum Gram/polygon feasibility condition, giving the leverage-only threshold \(\gamma(S)=U(\operatorname{diag}P_S)\) and \(\rho^*(S)=\sqrt{\gamma(S)}\); I spot-checked it against the note's own witnesses (pair space \(\gamma=(n-2)/2(n-1)=p/(n-1)\), \(S_{\mathrm{mid}}\) \(8/9\), \(S_{\mathrm{out}}\) \(1\)) and it is consistent and non-obvious. Everything around it delivers much less than the framing suggests: \(V^*(\rho;S)\) is NOT determined for general \(S\) — \ref{thm:exact-oracle-saddle} only recasts the definition as an exponential-size bilinear saddle via a standard finite minimax/separation argument, and its advertised "matching full-class converse" is definitional once \ref{lem:balanced-covariance-realizability} identifies the covariance image with \(\mathcal C_n\), not an independent lower bound. The regret headline is a bracket with multiplicative slack \(p/(n-1)\), which is loosest — a factor \(n-1\) — exactly in the leading application of a single external prognostic score (\(p=1\), rank-one \(S\)), so \(R^*(n,S)\) is effectively undetermined precisely where the motivation lives; moreover both bracket endpoints involve \(\kappa(S)\), which unlike \(\gamma(S)\) is admitted to require exponential enumeration, so these "certificates" are not score-matrix computable. Closed forms exist only for unequal two-block and homogeneous even-block partition subspaces, i.e. the classical stratified/matched-pair geometries, and \ref{thm:exact-pair-space-regret} is conceded to be a corollary of \ref{lem:pair-space-exact-frontier} rather than new content. Finally, because \(\gamma\) is shown to be a first-order slope at \(c_nP_H\) (the relint/affine-hull step), \(\rho>\rho^*(S)\) certifies only that SOME strictly positive, possibly infinitesimal, improvement over complete randomization exists — the note never quantifies the gain for general \(S\), so the practical screening claim is weaker than the TL;DR's "frontier" language implies. The framing is otherwise honest: the Honest scope section correctly disclaims polynomial-time and general closed forms, so I find no stale over-claim, only under-delivery relative to the ambition.
